description.narrative:
Impact objective:
All citizens and organizations in BiH access and benefit from transparent, fair, and democratic services based on accurate land, real estate and geospatial information provided by the Geodetic Authorities in cooperation with key stakeholders.
Outcome objectives per component:
Overall Capacity Development: Geodetic Agencies (GAs) are modern, transparent and efficient organizations contributing to economic and social development in close cooperation with stakeholders involved in land administration in BiH.
Mass Valuation: GAs contribute to a transparent property market by managing a real estate mass valuation system to benefit all citizens and the business community.
Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI): GAs and other spatial data providers enable service-based sharing of up-to-date and accurate spatial data used by stakeholders to face and resolve sustainable development challenges.
Geodetic Infrastructure: The accurate, reliable, and easily accessible geodetic infratructure is globally integrated and used by all stakeholders.

Detta projekt är utvecklat gemensamt av Federal Administration for Geodetic and Real Property Affairs (FGA) i Bosnien och Hercegovina (FBiH), Republic Authority for Geodetic and Property Legal Affairs (RGA) i Republika Srpska (RS) och Lantmäteriet i samarbete med Skatteverket.
De förväntade resultaten av projektet är: Övergripande kapacitetsutveckling: GA är moderna, transparenta och effektiva organisationer som bidrar till ekonomisk och social utveckling i nära samarbete med intressenter som är involverade i markförvaltningen i Bosnien och Hercegovina.
Massvärdering: GA bidrar till en transparent fastighetsmarknad genom att hantera ett massvärderingssystem för fastigheter till nytta för alla medborgare och näringslivet.
Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI): GA och andra rumsliga dataleverantörer möjliggör tjänstebaserad delning av aktuell och korrekt rumslig data som används av intressenter för att möta och lösa utmaningar inom hållbar utveckling.
Geodetisk infrastruktur: Den exakta, pålitliga och lättillgängliga geodetiska infrastrukturen är globalt integrerad och används av alla intressenter. .

This project is developed jointly by Federal Administration for Geodetic and Real Property Affairs (FGA) of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina (FBiH), Republic Authority for Geodetic and Property Legal Affairs (RGA) of the Republika Srpska (RS) and Lantmäteriet, The Swedish Mapping, Cadastral and Land Registration Authority in cooperation with the Swedish Tax Agency.
The expected outcomes of the project are: Overall Capacity Development: GA are modern, transparent and efficient organiza-tions contributing to economic and social development in close cooperation with stake-holders involved in land administration in BiH.
Mass Valuation: GA contribute to a transparent property market by managing a real estate mass valuation system to benefit all citizens and the business community.
Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI): GA and other spatial data providers enable service-based sharing of up-to-date and accurate spatial data used by stakeholders to face and resolve sustainable development challenges.
Geodetic Infrastructure: The accurate, reliable, and easily accessible geodetic infra-structure is globally integrated and used by all stakeholders.

Component 1 main focus has been on creating a strong project team, with both new and existing employees at the GA, and create an environment for capacity building within all components. 2024 was the first year of implementation, following the inception phase in 2023. A significant amount of time was invested in establishing the project management structure, recruiting 12 consultants (six per GA), and preparing internal project tools like the Project Operations Manual (POM). The recruitment process for these consultants was timeconsuming and experienced delays some consultants only started as late as August 2024. The recruitment was especially challenging in Republika Srpska. The DELEF project has had to adjust the approach significantly and this has slowed progress on this component. Activities to improve the ICT area and creation of communication plans for the GA were postponed. ICT and communication activities are multiyear in nature, and while initial discussions began late in 2024, no actual activities took place. The recruitment issues absorbed a lot of the project management's attention. Other notable results in this component include: A highlevel study visit to Sweden was conducted, resulting in improved political and institutional support for DELEFs objectives. Internal capacity building through onboarding training and planning workshops, including a MEL (Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning) approach has been delivered. For Component 2 all activities started according to the plan for 2024, but deliveries of methodologies and specifications for residential market, were delayed due to project consultant recruitment issues. The report notes that these delays are not considered critical at this stage, as the outputs are still achievable within the fiveyear project timeline. Notable results in this component include: Dedicated Mass Valuation teams were established in both RGA and FGA, with new staff trained and working groups functioning. Legal frameworks for Mass Valuation were adopted in both entities (RS and FBiH), and rulebooks were approved. Draft methodologies for data capture for residential property types (e.g., apartments and garages) were developed at FGA. RGA conducted a learning visit to Slovenia (GURS) to study a regional Mass Valuation model, initiating collaboration discussions. Enhanced engagement with the World Bank GIVE projectformal coordination began with an MoU signed in February 2024. In Component 3 all activities started according to the plan. Most activities are multiyear activities that will continue for several years. Due to challenges identifying technical experts at Lantmäteriet, activities for data dissemination and sharing and analyses of the current SDI Geoportal and Data Centre are delayed. Notable results under this component include: Both GA held successful SDI (spatial data infrastructure) Days (RGA in Banja Luka, FGA in Neum) with strong stakeholder participation and awarenessbuilding. FGA conducted 15 training sessions for SDI stakeholders on metadata, data management, and INSPIRE (Directive of the European Parliament establishing an Infrastructure for Spatial Information in the European Community) requirements. Joint learning visit to Sweden for SDI teams from both GAs, focusing on geoportal development and communication planning. Progress made in drafting SDI legal frameworks, especially by FGA, which proposed two new legal documents. Increased coordination and stakeholder inclusion across the SDI ecosystem in BiH and in regional forums (e.g., North Macedonia, Croatia). To summarise component 4, most activities are multiyear and will continue in 2025. One workshop aiming to train participants in transformation procedures was postponed until 2025. The project also decided to postpone a workshop for regional cooperation. For 2025, dialogues on how to proceed with RGAs participation in the component will continue. Notable results for 2024 include: Workshops were held with both GAs to analyze and structure data for geoid modelling, including quality review and followup steps. FGA completed complementary geodetic measurements and began planning for integration with European networks (EPN). FGA acquired Bernese GNSS software licenses and prepared for training in Switzerland in 2025. A detailed roadmap to establish an EPN station in FBiH was developed. Coordination and capacity building began for reference frame transformation and CORS network enhancements
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
